mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.4 million signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below $600 billion for three consecutive months signals a drawdown in household savings buffers, which increases reliance on credit and debt, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, which erodes real purchasing power and increases uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly housing starts (HOUST) and S&P 500 returns exists: above-average HOUST growth (> 1.5% month-over-month) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to anticipatory construction sector and broader economic optimism.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
